beats.text: You could be dead by tonight.
The most powerful man in Rome wrote that down to himself, every morning.
Marcus Aurelius — emperor, and Stoic — kept a private notebook we still read.
“Death hangs over thee: whilst yet thou livest, whilst thou mayest, be good.”
If this hour were your last — what pettiness would you drop? Who would you forgive?
Remember you will die. Then go and live.

source_note: Quote: Meditations IV.14, Meric Casaubon translation (1634), public domain.
